thread:
Hannah Li: quick update — atlas-4b-int4 onboarding smoke shows funcall parse failures ~12% on 500 samples. pattern differs from PTQ: we see more split-chunk malforms where the model outputs a partial object in one stream chunk and closes it in a later chunk, but occasional noise is inserted at the boundary.
Omar Singh: split-chunk meaning streaming boundary issues rather than trailing commas?
Hannah Li: correct. example stream (cleaned for chat): {tool:get args:{id:u1  then later  }} — concat usually fixes it but tokenization can insert a stray character or newline between chunks and break JSON.
Priya Rao: do we still see the usual trailing commas and lone backslashes?
Hannah Li: less trailing commas than PTQ; more inter-chunk control chars and occasional nullish token in the stitch point.
Victor Chen: how does this compare to fp32 and other quant formats?
Hannah Li: fp32 baseline ~0.2%; bridge-ptq runs show ~9% with trailing commas/backslashes; int4 variants show ~11-13% and the failures skew toward chunk-boundary corruption. different int4 compile flags shift the pattern.
Omar Singh: replay bundle available?
Hannah Li: uploaded: s3://canaries/atlas-int4/splitbound-repro-5467.jsonl (each line contains prompt, seed, compile_flags).
Priya Rao: any quick repro with streaming disabled?
Hannah Li: with streaming off, parse_fail drops to ~1.1% for the same seed set. suggests stitcher + tokenizer interplay.
Victor Chen: mitigation ideas?
Hannah Li: immediate options: 1) runtime concat-safe postproc that normalizes control chars and removes lone control tokens before parse, 2) force wrapped array output so partial pieces become elements and are easier to stitch, 3) disable streaming for canary to confirm cause.
Omar Singh: does retry help? temp=0 deterministic decode?
Hannah Li: simple retry recovers ~18% on a small set. concat-normalize postproc recovers ~65%. combo postproc+retry recovers ~86%.
Priya Rao: propose canary config draft:
canary_name: atlas-int4-splitbound-5467
model: atlas-4b-int4
cohorts:
  - name: streaming-on
    streaming: true
  - name: streaming-off
    streaming: false
  - name: streaming-on-postproc
    streaming: true
    rescue_pipeline: [concat_normalize, remove_ctrlchars, retry_temp0]
samples: 1200
record: [parse_fail_rate, recovery_by_step, token_diff, kernel_tag, tokenizer_version]
Omar Singh: add a small unit in the funcall harness that simulates chunk splits mid-escape and asserts parse recovery.
Victor Chen: also run an int4 compile variant toggling enable_fast_decoder and streaming_chunk_size to see if decoder kernel is implicated. capture kernel tag and tokenizer version per sample.
Hannah Li: will add token-level diffs and kernel tags to the canary instrumentation and launch cohorts this afternoon. initial summary in ~24h.
ci-bot: canary started: atlas-int4-splitbound-5467 | atlas-4b-int4 | cohorts=3 | samples=1200
Priya Rao: if split-boundary is confirmed as the dominant failure mode, gate int4 onboarding until we have either kernel/tokenizer fix or a robust runtime stitcher.
Hannah Li: agreed. will post curated failure examples and recovery signatures to the ticket and attach token diffs. thanks all
